title: Cogolin between old town, vineyards and marinas
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: Cogolin is one of the most transitional communes in the gulf. You move from old streets to the plain, from vineyards to the Mole valley, then to the marinas and harbour sectors.
content:
In Cogolin, the walk does not stay enclosed in the centre. The commune changes texture quickly. In only a few moves, you pass from older streets to vineyards, then to the valley and the maritime sectors.

A linking commune rather than a simple village

Cogolin is not best understood as an isolated hill village. Its interest lies in the continuity between the old core, cultivated sectors, the plain and the outlets towards the harbour and the marinas.

Vineyards and the valley give depth to the landscape

Around the centre, vineyards and the Mole valley recall a commune shaped by water, farming and circulation. That substance prevents Cogolin from being read as a mere coastal suburb.

The marinas change the end of the walk

Moving towards the maritime sectors, the commune opens out and takes another scale. This shift towards beach, harbour and boats does not erase the old town; it completes the personality of Cogolin instead.

This note extends the page Walking Through Cogolin. To continue within the same cluster, it also helps to open Cogolin, crafts, carpets, pipes and the old town.
